gloss: komusō; mendicant Zen monk who plays shakuhachi

definitions.gloss: komusō; mendicant Zen monk who plays shakuhachi
definitions.explanation: A Zen Buddhist monk of the Fuke sect who wandered while playing the {尺八|しゃくはち} shakuhachi flute as a form of spiritual practice. Recognizable in period dramas by a large basket-like straw hat ({天蓋|てんがい}) that covers the whole head.

examples.japanese: {虚無僧|こむそう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いていた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: A komusō was walking through the town.

examples.japanese: ⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{虚無僧|こむそう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{登場|とうじょう}→登場：13625_toujou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Komusō often appear in period dramas.

examples.japanese: {虚無僧|こむそう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{尺八|しゃくはち}→尺八：04465_shakuhachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}き→吹く：02445_fuku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{巡|めぐ}り→巡る：03930_meguru⟧⟦{修行|しゅぎょう}した→修行する：25391_shugyousuru⟧。
examples.english: Komusō traveled from place to place playing the shakuhachi as religious practice.

notes:
Members of the {普化宗|ふけしゅう} (Fuke) school of Zen, active mainly during the Edo period. They played the ⟦{尺八|しゃくはち}→尺八：04465_shakuhachi⟧ as {吹禅|すいぜん} ("blowing Zen")—meditation through breath and sound. The Fuke sect was abolished in 1871, but the iconic image of a tengai-hatted komusō remains a fixture of historical fiction.
